dedupe_keys.name: seismic performance and recovery of a community natural gas network centerville testbed

description: This study by Mohammad Reza Ameri and John van de Lindt of Colorado State University and the NIST-funded Center for Risk-Based Community Resilience Planning, published in the Journal of Performance of Constructed Facilities in 2019, models the seismic performance and recovery of a community natural gas network. Coverage: the virtual community Centerville, subjected to earthquakes of varying intensity from one point source through a well-known attenuation model; its gas network has a processing plant, compressor stations, city gate stations, district regulating stations and buried pipelines. Damage to components and their connectivity determines the functionality of supply nodes, assessed by Monte Carlo simulation, and functionality curves are presented for the network. The paper examines how the industrial make-up of the community and the replacement of conventional steel pipes affect gas recovery. Format and access: a journal article. Licence and cost: closed access, paid. Caveats: a virtual community, not a real network; the abstract was the part read. The damage and recovery approach can be reused for gas lifelines in community resilience and network flow models. It relates to the IN-CORE platform and its interdependent network functionality model in the catalogue.
